title: 2027-10-02 Mistral Dynamics Dedicated Capacity Intake
summary: Intro call to understand Mistral Dynamics' inference requirements across hosted, dedicated and private options. Primary focus on reserved GPU capacity, tenant isolation needs and burst integration with hosted fallback. Discussed latency targets, P99 SLOs, KV cache affinity and prewarm strategies; agreed to run a 2-week POC with benchmark payloads and follow-up security pack.
topics: Reserved GPU sizing and burst model
Isolation/topology: tenant fencing vs node pinning
Prewarm/warm pool strategies and KV cache affinity
Timeline for pilot and success criteria
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-02 16:00 UTC / Duration 48m / Redwood: Lena Park, Omar Singh / Mistral: Rajiv, Sophie, Marcus, Aisha

Summary: Quick intro, then deep dive into capacity and isolation options. Mistral runs two production services: realtime chat assistance (low latency, P99 < 90ms target) and nightly batch embeddings for search. They're sensitive about model data leakage and want tenant-level KV cache isolation for some customers.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, with Omar our SE. Could we go round quick intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Malhotra: Rajiv here, CTO at Mistral. Short timeline, want to validate a dedicated path for Q1.
[00:13] Sophie Lane: Sophie, head of ML — mostly curious about throughput and KV behaviours with long contexts.
[00:19] Marcus Yoon: Marcus, infra — network, k8s, VPC things.
[00:22] Aisha Patel: Aisha, security/compliance, SOC2/ISO questions.
[00:26] Omar Singh: Great, thanks. Quick high level: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Today we'll focus on Dedicated reserved capacity and how burst into Hosted could work if you need overflow.
[00:36] Lena Park: Also timeline and success criteria so we can map a POC.

[00:44] Sophie Lane: To kick off — our chat service needs consistent p99 latency < 90ms for 8k contexts, typical payload 512 tokens. We expect peak bursts (sales events) that are 4-5x baseline for 2-6 hours. Cost is a concern — so we want to balance reserved pool sizing vs burst to hosted.
[01:05] Omar Singh: Understood. Two levers: reserve enough GPU vRAM and prewarm warm-pools to hit latency; or right-size pool and route overflow to hosted API which has multi-tenant models. We also do KV caching & prefix cache — if cache affinity matters, prewarming specific model instances is possible.
[01:27] Marcus Yoon: On isolation, some customers require cryptographic tenancy — i.e., no shared KV cache. Can we guarantee tenant fencing?
[01:35] Omar Singh: Yes, we have options. On Dedicated we can do tenant-level isolation with node pinning or job-level containerized isolation. Node pinning guarantees KV cache containment but reduces bin-packing efficiency. There's also a hybrid — logical fencing with per-tenant namespaces and strict eviction policies.
[01:55] Rajiv Malhotra: What's the cost delta between full node pinning vs logical isolation? Ballpark.
[02:02] Omar Singh: Ballpark: node pinning increases unit cost ~20-40% depending on utilization because you lose bin-packing. Logical isolation is cheaper but requires stricter audit and tracing; for high security tenants we usually recommend node-level exclusivity.

[02:18] Sophie Lane: For our embedding batch jobs — they're less latency-sensitive but throughput heavy overnight. Can we multiplex those on same dedicated pool?
[02:26] Omar Singh: Yes, scheduling policies allow priority-based preemption. You can reserve a baseline throughput for realtime jobs and lower-priority batch jobs run in slack capacity. We also support separate GPU queues.

[02:38] Aisha Patel: KMS/HSM — we need to know key lifecycle and whether Redwood can integrate with our AWS KMS and on-prem HSM for private deployment. Also audit logs retention.
[02:49] Lena Park: We'll share the security whitepaper — but short answer: Dedicated + Private control plane supports customer-managed KMS; logs can be shipped to your SIEM and retention is configurable. Omar, do you want to add details?
[02:59] Omar Singh: Sure. For Private we offer connectors to AWS KMS and GCP KMS; HSM integrations are available for on-prem packages. Audit logs include token-level traces, model versioning and routing decisions; retention depends on the plan but we can meet typical enterprise requirements.

[03:20] Rajiv Malhotra: About bursting to hosted: is it transparent? We can't leak tenant-specific prompts to multi-tenant hosted models for regulated customers.
[03:29] Omar Singh: Good point. We support routing policies with allowlists — for regulated tenants you can block hosted fallback entirely. For mixed customers you can do non-sensitive traffic to hosted. Also, we can provision model variants on Hosted that are E2E isolated for partners in some regions (contracted).

[03:48] Sophie Lane: Operationally — how fast is a warm-pool prewarm? Our bursts are unpredictable — sometimes minutes after marketing sends out an email.
[03:55] Omar Singh: Warm pools can prewarm to a model in ~30-90s depending on model size and GPU topology. We also offer instant-scale via a small hot reserve and immediate fallback; for true minutes-level reaction we recommend a hybrid: prewarm heuristics + lightweight predictive warmers triggered by webhook from your traffic or release cadence.

[04:16] Marcus Yoon: How do you handle NUMA and MIG? We run some inference on MIG partitions for cost efficiency.
[04:22] Omar Singh: We support MIG and topology-aware scheduling. If you partition GPUs, expect throughput per-die differences. For small models MIG is efficient; for long-context chat with high KV cache and large memory, full-GPU shapes often perform better. We'll run benchmarks on your exact model builds.

[04:41] Rajiv Malhotra: Success criteria — for POC we'd like: 1) demonstrate p99 < 90ms for chat at 512 tokens, 2) validate tenant isolation for 2 flagged customers, 3) measure cost delta for reserve vs burst. Timeline: pilot in mid-October, maybe a 2-week run.
[04:59] Lena Park: Sounds good. We can do a 2-week dedicated POC: we'll provision a small reserved pool, replicate your request mix and share a benchmark dashboard.

[05:06] Sophie Lane: One more thing — model quantization. We have a slightly custom model fork. Can you serve quantized weights and keep compatibility with our special ops?
[05:14] Omar Singh: We onboard custom models; quantization support depends on op coverage. We have a model onboarding checklist and a short compatibility test. If we need custom kernels we can work with Research/Eng. For POC we'll run a quick compatibility pass.

[05:31] Aisha Patel: Can you confirm SOC2 and recent pen test reports? Also SSO — we use Okta and SAML.
[05:37] Lena Park: We'll attach our SOC2 report and current penetration test summary. SSO via SAML/Okta supported; role-based access (RBAC) available at route, model and token granularity.

[05:47] Rajiv Malhotra: Ok, what about pricing — especially reserved commitment vs on-demand token pricing. We need a simple model to evaluate ROI.
[05:55] Lena Park: We'll send a tailored cost model. Typically reserved pricing is a capacity commit (monthly) plus usage delta; bursting to hosted is billed at hosted rates for overflow. We'll break down per-token and per-GPU hour for your workload and show break-even points.

[06:10] Marcus Yoon: Are there any preemption risks? We need a SLA and avoidance of noisy neighbor impact.
[06:16] Omar Singh: With Dedicated reserved pools you don't get preempted by other customers. Noisy neighbor inside your tenant depends on your internal tenancy patterns; we can set quotas and cgroups to isolate your jobs. For multi-tenant within your org, node pinning stops interference.

[06:30] (brief cross talk)
[06:33] Sophie Lane: If we choose node pinning for two high security customers, can we still use logical isolation for the rest to save costs?
[06:39] Omar Singh: Absolutely — hybrid mix is common. Pin the handful of high-risk customers, keep others in logical namespaces. We'll model the economics.

[06:48] Rajiv Malhotra: Any gotchas for VPC egress costs if we run Private?
[06:52] Lena Park: Egress patterns depend on your topology, but yes you should account for inter-region egress if you cross clouds. We'll factor that into the cost model.

[06:59] Marcus Yoon: For the POC do you need us to provide datasets or synthetic traces?
[07:03] Lena Park: Synthetic traces are fine for initial run; for the isolation test we'll need redacted real customer prompts for fidelity. Sophie, is that feasible?
[07:11] Sophie Lane: We can produce redacted traces and a representative distribution.

[07:15] Rajiv Malhotra: Last — fallback behaviours on model rollouts. We can't have sudden regressions.
[07:20] Omar Singh: We support canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous model version if quality or latency regressions detected, and eval hooks. We'll include a release gate in the POC.

[07:31] Lena Park: Great — let's recap actions and next steps.

[07:35] Rajiv Malhotra: Thanks — useful call.

End of transcript.
